issues.detail: Install commands lean on macOS Homebrew and a Linux tarball without a full Windows path, and the setup assumes Ollama and Python rather than being agent-agnostic.

scenarios.name: air-gapped-model-transfer
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric's flow of pulling both models on a connected machine and copying ~/.ollama/models (and mentions the Docker volume), sets OLLAMA_HOST, verifies with ollama list, and calls for an offline test; A omits the Docker volume copy, uses a throwaway-server export approach that deviates from the plain pull-and-copy flow, and gives no explicit disconnected-network test beyond a smoke test, though it is otherwise thorough on firewalling and bind verification.

scenarios.name: sqlite-kb-with-fts-and-embeddings
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it has a documents table, a chunks table with a BLOB embedding column, an FTS5 table with content=, an explicit FTS 'rebuild' after loading, /api/embed with nomic-embed-text, packed floats, cosine similarity, and an /api/generate RAG prompt that says to answer ONLY from the context. A has no documents table and no explicit 'rebuild' (it uses triggers), it normalizes vectors and uses a dot product instead of an explicit cosine function, and it uses /api/chat instead of /api/generate, though it does use /api/embed, packed floats, and an ONLY-from-excerpts system prompt.

scenarios.name: scale-and-hardware-tuning
scenarios.rationale: A hits every rubric point: phi3:mini, the 50k brute-force limit with sqlite-vec at 200k, an FTS5 MATCH fallback on fts_documents, and re-embedding if the model changes. B recommends other models, says brute force holds up at 200k, never mentions sqlite-vec, and uses its own FTS table, though it does cover model mismatch and BM25 fallback.
